prompt: A staircase rises $6$ units while running $2$ units across. What is the slope (rise over run)?
hint: Slope compares how far something goes up with how far it goes across. Which two numbers in the story are those?

hints.text: Slope compares how far something goes up with how far it goes across. Which two numbers in the story are those?
The rise is $6$ and the run is $2$, so set up rise over run as $\frac{6}{2}$ and divide.
$6 \div 2 = 3$, so the slope of the staircase is $3$.

explanation: Slope is defined as rise over run, so write the rise of $6$ over the run of $2$: $\frac{6}{2}$.
Carry out the division to turn the fraction into one number: $6 \div 2 = 3$.
The slope is $3$, which means the stairs climb $3$ units for every $1$ unit across.

alternativeExplanations.title: Shrink the staircase
steps: $6$ up over $2$ across is the same steepness as $3$ up over $1$ across.
The "up per one across" number IS the slope: $3$.
